title: Hadamard-type inequalities for hyperbolic polynomials
statement:
Let $P$ be a homogeneous, real, symmetric, hyperbolic polynomial of degree $k$ on $F?$. Let $AF?M_n(F?)$. If the eigenvalue vector $F? (A)F?\Gamma(P)$, then $(a_{11},\ldots,a_{nn})F?\Gamma(P)$ and

$$
P(a_{11},\ldots,a_{nn})\geq P(\lambda(A)).
$$

**Hadamard-type inequality for hyperbolic polynomials.** The claim extends the diagonal-versus-eigenvalue inequality from elementary symmetric polynomials to homogeneous, real, symmetric, hyperbolic polynomials. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
source_name: Nam Q. Le, “Hadamard-type inequalities for k-positive matrices”, arXiv:2112.01462 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01462

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

title: Signed mean value trace inequalities for Hermitian matrices
statement:
Let $\mathsfsl{A},\mathsfsl{B},\mathsfsl{C}\in\mathbb{H}^{d}$ be Hermitian matrices, let $q$ be a positive integer, and let $s>0$. For a Hermitian matrix $\mathsfsl{X}$, write $\mathsfsl{X}_+$ and $\mathsfsl{X}_-$ for its positive and negative parts, and write $|\mathsfsl{X}|$ for its absolute value. **Signed mean value trace inequalities.** The following inequalities should hold:

$$
\operatorname{tr}\big[\mathsfsl{C}(\mathrm{e}^{\mathsfsl{A}}-\mathrm{e}^{\mathsfsl{B}})\big]\leq \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}\big[((s(\mathsfsl{A}-\mathsfsl{B})_+^2+s^{-1}\mathsfsl{C}_+^2)\mathrm{e}^{\mathsfsl{A}}+(s(\mathsfsl{A}-\mathsfsl{B})_-^2+s^{-1}\mathsfsl{C}_-^2)\mathrm{e}^{\mathsfsl{B}})\big]
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{tr}\big[\mathsfsl{C}(\mathsfsl{A}^{q}-\mathsfsl{B}^{q})\big]\leq \frac{q}{2}\operatorname{tr}\big[((s(\mathsfsl{A}-\mathsfsl{B})_+^2+s^{-1}\mathsfsl{C}_+^2)|\mathsfsl{A}|^{q-1}+(s(\mathsfsl{A}-\mathsfsl{B})_-^2+s^{-1}\mathsfsl{C}_-^2)|\mathsfsl{B}|^{q-1})\big].
$$

These inequalities would provide the missing ingredient for extending the paper's concentration method to matrix self-bounding functions. The source presents them as needed for that analysis, but gives no resolution, so their status remains open.
source_name: Daniel Paulin, Lester Mackey and Joel A. Tropp, “Deriving Matrix Concentration Inequalities from Kernel Couplings”, arXiv:1305.0612 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0612

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

title: The coefficient-of-variation bound for fast mRNA–microRNA dynamics
statement:
Let $\rho_\text{fast}^{\delta,\gamma,p}$ denote the fast-regime distribution and let $\rho_0^{\delta}$ denote the corresponding free-mRNA distribution, with $\mathrm{CV}$ their coefficients of variation. **Coefficient-of-variation bound.** For any $\delta>1$ and $\gamma,p>0$, one has

$$
\mathrm{CV}(\rho_\text{fast}^{\delta,\gamma,p})\leq\mathrm{CV}(\rho_0^{\delta}).
$$

This would assert that, outside the asymptotic regimes discussed immediately beforehand, binding and production of microRNA do not increase the coefficient of variation relative to free mRNAs. The source presents it as the theoretical result one would like to have; no proof or resolution is supplied here.
source_name: Pierre Degond, Maxime Herda and Sepideh Mirrahimi, “A Fokker-Planck approach to the study of robustness in gene expression”, arXiv:2006.14985 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.14985

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

title: Shifted-binomial log-concavity conjecture for Plücker coefficients
statement:
Let $\lambda=(2^{e_2},\ldots,m^{e_m})$ be a partition without parts equal to $1$, and set

$$
N:=|\lambda|,\qquad M:=|\widetilde\lambda|,
$$

where $\widetilde\lambda$ is obtained by subtracting $1$ from each part. Write the Plücker expansion

$$
[\overline Y_\lambda(d)]=\sum_{\lceil M/2\rceil\le i\le M}P_{\lambda;i}(d)s_{i,M-i}.
$$

Set $d=N+x$, define $Q_{\lambda;i}(x):=P_{\lambda;i}(N+x)$, and expand

$$
Q_{\lambda;i}(x)=\sum_{r\ge0}C_{\lambda;i,r}\binom xr.
$$

**Shifted-binomial log-concavity conjecture.** For every partition $\lambda$ without parts equal to $1$, and every admissible index $i$, the sequence $(C_{\lambda;i,0},C_{\lambda;i,1},C_{\lambda;i,2},\ldots)$ is nonnegative and log-concave. Equivalently, $C_{\lambda;i,r}\ge0$ and

$$
C_{\lambda;i,r}^2\ge C_{\lambda;i,r-1}C_{\lambda;i,r+1},
$$

with $C_{\lambda;i,r}=0$ outside the degree range of $Q_{\lambda;i}$. The conjecture concerns a shifted binomial refinement of positivity and log-concavity for Plücker coefficients; the source gives no resolution status.
source_name: Gergely Bérczi and László M. Fehér, “Positivity in classical enumerative geometry: a case study in synchronized AI-assisted mathematics”, arXiv:2605.25271 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25271

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).
